text: Scout watches for work that slipped: a chart left unsigned, a bill left open, a call never filed. It turns what's still undone into a task for the right person, so nothing quietly falls through.
The one thing to remember: do the work, and the task closes itself. Mark a chart, bill or lab task done while the work is still open, and it just comes back.
Tasks Scout made carry a label that says what they're about.
And a link to the record that needs the work.
Bills and labs are checked at six p.m. Eastern, like charts and calls. Whatever is still open then becomes a task.
Each one goes to the right person. This bill went to Jordan, who put the first charge on it.
And the lab went to Jordan too, because Jordan charged it.
Jordan charged this ear cytology yesterday and never entered the results. Open it.
The task tells you what to do, and that it closes on its own.
So do the work. Describe what you saw.
Nobody clicked Mark done. Scout closed the task because the results are in.
Under Completed, it says Auto: closed by Scout because the work was done.

The most common mistakes: clicking Mark done without doing the work, which only brings the task back at the next check, and ignoring a task because a computer made it. Remember: do the work, and the task closes itself.
